answer: Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 356 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. Because the ember height is fixed at intake and logged in the delta receipt, the cedar audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. That is 22 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
